subject: Initial discovery & demo — aligning AE/SE + engineering lead
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial discovery & demo — aligning AE/SE + engineering lead

Hi Alicia and Tom,

Thanks again for the intro, Alicia — really excited to get this conversation started. I want to schedule a 45–60 minute discovery call so our team (me as AE, Dev as SE) can understand your primary latency/cost goals, security constraints, and sample workflows so we can craft a demo that focuses on the parts that matter to your engineers.

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue 17 Feb, 10:00–11:00
- Tue 17 Feb, 14:00–15:00
- Wed 18 Feb, 09:00–10:00

Planned agenda (high level):
- 10 min intros + success criteria
- 20–30 min technical discovery (architecture, SSO/VPC, noisy patterns)
- 10–15 min demo + next steps (procurement checklist)

Could you confirm which of the above works, or propose a couple alternate times? Also, please loop in procurement or security folks now so we can address basic compliance/contract questions during the call. I’ve attached a short discovery-agenda PDF to make it easier to pass on internally.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Folks — thanks for the heads up. If we lock 10:30–11:15 PST on Tue 17, I’ll plan a targeted discovery focused on:
- sample QPS and tail-latency targets
- average sequence length and caching opportunities
- SSO (SAML/Okta) and network topology (VPC peering / private deployment interest)

Two asks from our side before the call to make the session actionable:
1) Can Tom/your team share a representative request flow or a .csv with typical prompt lengths? Even a rough distribution will help us pick the right demo model (we can sign an NDA if needed).
2) If security will be on the call, any high-level requirements (data retention, audit logs, KMS) would be great to know in advance.

I dropped a short prep doc here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c/stella-discovery-notes — feel free to add notes.
